reasoning: Started from the approved quarterly driver set (kept exactly; my disagreements are in gap_note) and looked for what makes consensus wrong on the downside. Evidence found: (1) insiders sold ~$1.09B of stock May-Oct 2026 across 90 Form 4s with no open-market purchase (Slootman $731M, Dageville $175M, Speiser $85M, Kleinerman $46M, Garrett $43M) [25,30]; mostly 10b5-1 and founder/director diversification, so a weak signal on fundamentals but a steady supply overhang. (2) Credit: $3.75B 0% converts (conversion ~500/484, capped calls to 820.30, cost 383.5) plus ~286M premium to retire 261.8 of 2027 notes [10,26]; principal now 5.79B vs 7.10B cash, so the balance sheet is fine (net cash 1.31B) but the cash is no longer 'excess', and the 2027/2029 notes are in the money (~10M shares in the guide). No covenant or rating issue. (3) Litigation: four unaccrued matters (two 10b-5 suits, breach MDL with standing upheld, LLM copyright class) [7,27,32]; small in expected value (~-0.2/share). (4) Accounting/quality: GAAP operating loss TTM -1,237M [F13] with SBC 1,642M [F46]; FCF less SBC is negative (-447M TTM); the Q2 FY27 'new customer' residual jump (7.9% of product revenue) includes Observe/Natoma acquisitions and TTM lag; cRPO covers only ~69% of the set's NTM product revenue and total RPO fell 9.77B -> 9.00B since Q4 FY26 [7], so the NRR path rests on uncontracted on-demand consumption. (5) Competition: Databricks >$7B run-rate, >80% growth, SQL warehousing >$1.5B >100% [28]; Iceberg flagged by the company itself as reducing lock-in [7]. Weighed honestly: the beat record (10/10 product and margin) and AI consumption acceleration are real, and none of the bear items is a smoking gun; the downside case is mostly a multiple story. Valuation: EV/sales is the only multiple that works with GAAP losses (METHOD FIT weakens GAAP P/E and EV/EBITDA, which I do not use, and partly EV/sales because it ignores SBC), so I added a 10%-weight SBC-burdened earnings-power leg (99). Peer proxy median 6.55x (6 peers, flagged), own 14.3x, k=0.8 rule 12.2x, cut to 11.0x (judgment for Kilian, ~-9% of value). Research target (12m) 264.36 (engine), downside (P10) 142.55, upside (P90) 380.97: a fatter left tail, consistent with 64% realized vol and the 118-385 range. Consensus targets sit far above (Street mean ~$424 late Sep [26]); I am ~11% below spot. Research limits: Twelve Data analyst/insider endpoints unavailable on this plan; 6 page fetches used (budget); several lane sources (Trefis, 24/7 Wall St. margin and short-candidate pieces, Levi Korsinsky notice) are cited only for what their titles state. Lane share: 13 of 43 sources are lane-type; excluding the 23 sources inherited from the approved set (basic reported facts) and 9 data pages, 10 of 11 are in lane. Not driver-linked: the custom SBC-burdened leg. ROUND 2: the supervisor found (a) my 1.2x haircut below the k-rule had no tested evidence: now 12.62x on a cleaned EV/NTM consensus median (7.14x, TDC out); (b) the SBC leg's 0.1 weight had no support: now 0; (c) my FCF guide record was unscored: FY25 miss (29% -> 26%), FY26 inside (25% -> 25.5%). I also took depreciation-only D&A (2.4%; amortization is already outside non-GAAP EBIT), capex 1.5% and buybacks 600/700. The skeptic case stays in the distribution: downside 187 at ~6.9x, thesis break 185. Research target (12m) 264.36 -> 323.77.

drivers.label: Net revenue retention rate (company definition: trailing-2-year cohort of capacity customers, product revenue year 2 / year 1; reported at quarter end)
drivers.source: Ex.99.1 'Financial Highlights' / Key Business Metrics: Q1 FY26 124%, Q2 125%, Q3 125%, Q4 125% [1-4], Q1 FY27 126% [5], Q2 FY27 126% [6] (10-Q: 126% at 2026-07-31 vs 125% at 2026-01-31 [7]); history Q4 FY24 131% [11], FY25 128/127/127/126% [12-15]. Definition: cohort = capacity customers using the platform in the first month of the first year of the trailing 2 years; NRR = cohort product revenue year 2 / year 1; churned customers count as zero [6].
drivers.derivation: Identity (per Kilian's spec): product revenue(q) = product revenue(same quarter a year earlier) x nrr + new_cust. Q3 FY27 128%, Q4 129%: the reported rate is trailing-12-month and lags the quarters (quarterly product growth 33.9%/36.8% in Q1/Q2 FY27 vs TTM product growth 31.1%/32.6% and NRR 126% [5,6]; the Q3 guide is +37-38% y/y [6]), so the TTM rate rises as H2 FY27 rolls in (CFO: third consecutive quarter of acceleration, existing-customer consumption is the driver [6,7]). FY28 129/127.5/126/124.5%: the AI step-up (CoCo 9,100 accounts, +2,000 in Q2 [6]) laps. FY29 123->120%, FY30 119->117%: the fade the company showed as the base grew (131% Q4 FY24 -> 124% Q1 FY26 [11,1]) plus Iceberg tables (storage and some compute outside Snowflake, 10-Q risk factor [7]), Databricks warehousing ($1.5B, >100% growth [23]) and price-performance cuts passed through. Check: the TTM residual implied by our quarters is 6.0% of TTM product revenue at Q4 FY27, 5.2% Q4 FY28, 3.9% Q4 FY29, 3.1% Q4 FY30 (FY25-FY26 actual 2.8-3.2%, Q2 FY27 5.0%): the FY28 reported rate could run ~1-2 pt above this path at the same revenue. Variant: downside -4 pt, upside +3 pt on every forecast quarter (scenarios).
drivers.why: The consumption metric the company and the Street use for existing-customer growth; the debated item (AI consumption up, Iceberg/storage and price cuts down).

drivers.label: Product revenue not explained by NRR: customers outside the NRR cohort (new logos of the last ~24 months, on-demand) + acquisitions ($M a quarter; identity residual)
drivers.derivation: Q3 FY27 135, Q4 110: the H1 FY27 residual (78, 118) is not all new-customer revenue: it holds the TTM lag of NRR (quarterly existing-customer growth runs ahead of the TTM rate) and Observe; as the TTM NRR catches up (128-129%) the residual falls back. FY28 80/72/68/66, FY29 66-70, FY30 70-74 = 2.3-3.0% of product revenue, the FY25-FY26 structural level (quarterly residual 1.4-4.9%, mean 2.9%; TTM 2.8-3.2%), growing slowly with net customer adds (616-740 a quarter [4,7,8]). Variant: downside -25%, upside +20%.
drivers.why: Keeps the NRR identity closed: every dollar of product revenue is either existing-cohort (nrr) or this residual; makes new-logo and acquisition revenue visible.
